newsitem.title: CHINA: HK, China check report on Spratlys fishermen.
newsitem.headline: HK, China check report on Spratlys fishermen.

text.p: China's Foreign Ministry office in Hong Kong said on Tuesday it was checking reports that Philippine authorities had detained 23 Hong Kong Chinese fishermen near the disputed Spratly Islands in the South China Sea.
"We are now trying to understand the situation with the parties involved," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman declined to comment further.
Philippine Navy officials said earlier on Tuesday that the 23 fishermen were detained near the Spratlys on July 31, reports from Manila said.
The fishermen were near Hasahasa Shoal, about 145 km (90 miles) west of the southwestern Philippine island of Palawan, when they were apprehended, said a Navy official who asked not to be identified.
There was no official explanation from Manila for the delay in reporting the detention of the fishermen, who are being held in Puerto Princesa, capital of Palawan Island province.
The Hong Kong government said it had no information about the arrests and would check with China's Foreign Ministry office.
"So far, we have not received any information or request of assistance in respect of the alleged arrest," a Hong Kong government spokeswoman said.
"We will check with parties including the Foreign Ministry office in Hong Kong for more information," she said.

Hong Kong, a former British colony, is now an autonomous part of China with a free hand to run its internal affairs, but foreign affairs are handled by Beijing's Foreign Ministry Commissioner in the territory.
The Spratlys are a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals some or all of which are claimed by China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
Beijing says all the islands and rocky outcrops in the sea have historically belonged to China since ancient times.
A series of recent incidents involving Chinese naval and fishing vessels in areas claimed by Manila has threatened to sour relations between China and the Philippines.

In May, the Philippine Navy arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near Scarborough Shoal, well north of the Spratlys, for illegal entry. A local judge dismissed the charges and ordered their release after 52 days in detention.
The judge said ownership of the shoal had not been established so there were no grounds to charge them with illegally entering Philippine waters.
